rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for an unexpected event or outcome, especially a neutral one.

example.english: This power outage was a real surprise.
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 ting4 din6 zan1 hai6 ji3 ngoi6

rows.note: Use this for a pleasant surprise or the accompanying feeling of delighted surprise.

example.english: Getting a cake from my friends on my birthday was a real surprise.
example.traditional: 生日嗰日收到朋友送嘅蛋糕，真係驚喜。
example.jyutping: saang1 jat6 go2 jat6 sau1 dou2 pang4 jau5 sung3 ge3 daan6 gou1 zan1 hai6 ging1 hei2

rows.jyutping: gaau2 dou3 A hou2 ji3 ngoi6
rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken way to say that something causes A to be surprised or caught off guard.

example.english: They suddenly said I didn't need to work overtime, which was a surprise to me.
example.traditional: 佢突然話唔使我加班，搞到我好意外。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dat6 jin4 waa6 m4 sai2 ngo5 gaa1 baan1 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 hou2 ji3 ngoi6

rows.note: Use this when the surprise startles or frightens A, rather than pleasantly surprising them.

example.english: You shouted loudly behind me and gave me a nasty surprise!
example.traditional: 你突然喺我後面大嗌，嚇親我喇！
example.jyutping: nei5 dat6 jin4 hai2 ngo5 hau6 min6 daai6 ngaai3 haak3 can1 ngo5 laa3

rows.note: Use this nominal form for the feeling of astonishment itself, especially when it is neutral or unpleasant rather than pleasant.

example.english: This result caused surprise for everyone.
example.traditional: 呢個結果令大家都感到驚訝。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 git3 gwo2 ling6 daai6 gaa1 dou1 gam2 dou3 ging1 ngaa6

rows.note: Use this when deliberately giving A a pleasant surprise, such as turning up unexpectedly.

example.english: We deliberately didn't tell you because we wanted to surprise you.
example.traditional: 我哋特登唔話你知，想畀你驚喜。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 dak6 dang1 m4 waa6 nei5 zi1 soeng2 bei2 nei5 geng1 hei2
